QUESTION OF THE WEEK - A full survey of first quarter GDP forecasts was conducted ahead of the release of the data next Wednesday. Economists generally expect a stronger quarterly figure than December but a weaker annual figure, reflecting the dropping out of last March's 1.6 percent quarterly rise. Full details are tabled seperately. As well, ahead of the Reserve Bank board meeting on Tuesday, economists were asked what chance they saw of there being a fifth cut in official interest rates this cycle. The median is below 50 percent, but there are a few economists up at, or above, 50 percent. Some at around 40 percent said the bias to their forecasts was to the topside, and the activity data over the next few months would be the key. ----------------------------------------------------------------

BUILDING APPROVALS - After falling in four of the last five months, economists are expecting the April data to show a small rise. Like retail trade, approvals started the year of strongly but have since stumbled, and if growth is to pick up later this year, signs of housing strength will need to appear in the June quarter, economists said.

FOREIGN DEBT - A slight fall in the Australian dollar against the U.S. dollar over the March quarter and A$1.6 billion of debt financing of the March quarter capital account has led to expectations that the net dbet has risen slightly. Working against the debt rise is that the Australian dollar strengthened over the quarter in trade weighted terms.
